claim: Within one case, human physicians mix forward and backward reasoning; no protocol is purely one direction (Patel, Arocha, Groen 1987; Arocha and Patel 1991).
agent_test: Label each trace step finding-to-hypothesis or hypothesis-to-finding; check that mixed traces are the norm, not pure ones, for the agent.

claim: Forward-directed reasoning is more common on familiar cases and for higher expertise; backward or hypothetico-deductive reasoning rises on hard or unfamiliar cases, for experts too.
agent_test: Measure direction share vs case difficulty at equal tokens; expect more backward use on hard items.

claim: Expert vs novice direction difference is a matter of degree: experts use scheme-inductive or pattern recognition about 90% of the time vs over 50% for novices (gastroenterology, 20 v 20); novices also use forward reasoning often.
agent_test: Not testable directly; background only.

claim: Using forward (pattern/scheme) reasoning goes with higher diagnostic accuracy in humans, but the link is correlational and confounded with expertise and case difficulty.
agent_test: Regress accuracy on direction share controlling for difficulty on agent traces.

claim: Forced analysis of an initial hypothesis raised accuracy about 31-40% to 65-70% in nephrologists and residents; 96% of changes were wrong-to-right (N=15, 10 cases).
agent_test: Force a second-pass hypothesis check on the first answer; compare accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: The best reasoning direction depends on expertise: scheme-inductive (forward) priming helped residents (OR 5.69) but not experienced nephrologists (OR 0.57, CI crossing 1).
agent_test: Weak; would need per-difficulty tests of direction instruction on the agent.

claim: Telling clinicians to be slow and reflective, or to take a second look, does not improve diagnosis over being fast; structured content-bearing checks help more than generic prompts. LLMs show the same split: generic self-review hurt (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1) and a generic warning raised MedEinst trap rate (43.46 to 60.50), while a cue naming the source's reliability recovered accuracy.
agent_test: Compare generic 'reflect' prompt vs a check naming a specific alternative, at equal tokens.

claim: A differential checklist helps only if it contains the correct diagnosis (accuracy 0.75 v 0.49 control); a checklist missing the truth gave 0.43 (p=0.602 vs control). In LLMs, a misleading clinician differential lowered correct-diagnosis inclusion in 14 of 21 models (mean -5.4 points, GPT-4o -29.8).
agent_test: Offer the agent a candidate list with and without the truth; check for harm when absent.

claim: For novices, a diagnosis-first (backward-style) aid beat a feature-first forward tool; the forward tool did not beat control (d=0.714 Atlas v ORAD). Forward tools can fail through wrong filters (80 of 152 errors).
agent_test: Compare feature-first vs hypothesis-first prompting for weak models; count errors that exclude the truth early.

claim: A forward step plus a backward check (what findings should I see if diagnosis d were true) improves LLM differential diagnosis modestly on text: Dual-Inf +6.1 points over SC-CoT (GPT-4, 570 notes) and +4.8 to +5.9 on GPT-4o, Llama3-70B and BioLlama3-70B; MSDiagnosis +2.28 final F1. No compute-matched comparison exists.
agent_test: Add an expected-findings check to the agent; compare to a same-token self-consistency baseline.

claim: The backward check may cost accuracy of detail: Dual-Inf raised reported factual errors (8.2 to 17 per 100 cases) while cutting missing content, but that comparison is against SC-CoT, not against its own ablations, so the backward module is not shown to cause it. MSDiagnosis gains are within about 2 points across ablations and untested for significance.
agent_test: Track factual-error rate alongside accuracy when adding backward checks.

claim: Early errors propagate: final diagnosis quality depends on the first (forward) answer in a multi-step LLM pipeline.
agent_test: Log first-answer vs final-answer agreement; test a pre-commitment delay of the first hypothesis.

claim: Strong LLMs show Einstellung-like anchoring: trap rates above 50% for frontier and top-accuracy rows on counterfactual pairs (the paper's text and Table 1 disagree on which models have the top accuracy). A forward-evidence plus backward-counterfactual agent cut trap rate (Qwen3-32B 43.46 to 38.32 with the causal graph, 33.75 with memory). No shadow-penalty-only ablation exists.
agent_test: Build trap pairs (same prior, one discriminating fact) and measure trap rate with and without a shadow-evidence penalty.

claim: Prompting a model to imitate a clinician reasoning style does not raise accuracy (GPT-4 MedQA 76% CoT vs 78% differential, P=0.24; GPT-3.5 lower for differential, analytic, Bayesian).
agent_test: Reconfirms: do not add style personas; test only if cheap.

claim: Backward verification gives small gains in math (FOBAR +2.1, +1.8; self-verification +2.33 avg) and large relative gains in closed logic proof search (LAMBADA +37% to +113% at depth 5).
agent_test: Use goal-to-facts search only for closed formal sub-problems; verify by masked-fact recovery on arithmetic-like items.

claim: Giving physicians an LLM did not improve their diagnostic reasoning (76% v 74%), while the LLM alone scored 16 points higher; a UK replication (n=22) agrees in direction; a 2026 meta-analysis finds no significant LLM vs human difference.
agent_test: Background; shows human-AI interface matters more than direction.

claim: No LLM study found directly tests the Patel-Groen claim (expert forward, novice backward) in models; forward and backward in LLM papers are engineering labels.
agent_test: A direct test is open: manipulate direction instruction by case difficulty.

claim: The 1986 founding result rests on seven cardiologists and one endocarditis case (abstract read): accurate diagnosers reasoned purely forward, inaccurate ones mixed forward and backward. Per-group counts are still unverified, and later reviews say hypothetico-deductive use does not explain the novice-expert transition.
agent_test: Cite as N=7, one case. Do not quote per-group counts.

claim: Multiple-choice answer options induce backward reasoning (from options) in exams; forward reasoning from stem data dominates (FR>BR); high scorers use both more (OR 3.33 FR, 2.67 BR; N=210).
agent_test: Test whether the agent reasons from options first on multiple choice and whether blind-first generation helps.

claim: Direction shifts within a case: early inquiry backward/hypothesis-driven, later confirmatory forward (cognitive zipper); experts read later findings as support for early diagnosis.
agent_test: Check if agent trace stages show this shift; qualitative model only.

claim: Misleading hypotheses supplied up front harm LLM diagnosis in a model-dependent way: more thinking budget cut the loss in GPT-5 (10.4 to 1.7-4.4 points) and Qwen3 (11.7 to 3.9) but not in Claude Sonnet 4.5 or Gemini-3-Pro, which lost little anyway.
agent_test: Run the agent with a wrong supplied differential at several thinking budgets; measure the loss.

claim: A cue that tells the model how reliable the supplied hypothesis is (clinician uncertain or inexperienced) recovered the accuracy lost to misleading input while keeping the gain from expert input (GPT-5, Gemini 3 Flash; partial in Claude Sonnet 4.5).
agent_test: Tag every hypothesis with its source and reliability; compare to untagged.

claim: Generic self-review without external evidence does not help LLMs and can hurt (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 after one round; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 after two); with oracle knowledge of errors it helps strongly.
agent_test: Replace any reflect step with a check that names a finding to look for.

claim: Answer options change LLM behaviour: option-ID selection bias persists under polite debiasing instructions, and open-style questions score about 25% below MCQ on average. Effect of option-first versus blind-first diagnosis in medicine is untested.
agent_test: Compare blind-first differential with option-first answers on a diagnosis set.

claim: Reasoning models give factually sound diagnostic reasoning (factuality above 90%) but miss key steps and are weaker at choosing which examinations to request (best recall 43.61%); diagnosis accuracy rises from 71.79% to 89.76% (R1) as findings are supplied. Their traces were not coded for direction.
agent_test: Label forward and backward steps in reasoning-model traces by case difficulty.

claim: Expertise explained by stored knowledge structure (encapsulation, illness scripts) is the main rival to a reasoning-direction account; debate on the role of biomedical knowledge remains open.
agent_test: None; background only.
